patterns.comment: A branch target. Labels end in a colon and are named on branch instructions.
patterns.name: keyword.control.mi.label

patterns.comment: The MI instruction set, ordered longest-first so that a longer instruction matches before a shorter one sharing its prefix. A few entries have no page in the current IBM reference (CMPSWP, DEQWAIT, EDITPD, LBCPYNV, LBCPYNVR, LBEDIT, MATMATR1, MATOBJLCK, MATQMSGQ, MEMUSEHINT, MODS1, MODS2, QUANTIZEBE, QUANTIZEBV); MATOBJLCK and MATQMSGQ look like misspellings of MATOBJLK and MATQMSG, which are now listed alongside them. The extended forms are included: an instruction may carry B for the branch form, I for the indicator form, S for the short form and R for rounding, in combination, so ADDN also appears as ADDNB, ADDNBR, ADDNBS and the rest. Each was taken from its own op code table.

patterns.comment: Short instructions that would otherwise match inside a longer word, so they require leading whitespace.
patterns.name: keyword.other.mi

patterns.comment: Program structure statements: ENTRY, DCL, PARM_LIST, PARM, PEND and EXT.
patterns.name: keyword.other.mi

patterns.comment: Arithmetic, comparison and concatenation operators written as symbols.
patterns.name: keyword.other.mi

patterns.comment: A bare asterisk, used as the entry point name and as a null operand.
patterns.name: keyword.other.mi

patterns.comment: Backslash escape inside a quoted literal. IBM i literals escape an apostrophe by doubling it rather than with a backslash, so this rule appears to be vestigial.
patterns.name: constant.character.escape.mi

patterns.comment: Storage class and declaration attributes: AUTO automatic storage, STATIC static storage, BAS based on a pointer, BASPCO based on that pointer with an offset, BDRY an alignment boundary, DEF defined over another declaration, INIT an initial value, DIM a dimension. BASPCO comes before BAS so the longer word wins. PARM and EXT are attributes too, but the program structure rule already matches them. Source as for the declaration types: Svalgaard, MI Programming.
patterns.name: storage.modifier.mi

patterns.comment: Declaration types: SPCPTR a space pointer, SYSPTR a system pointer, INSPTR an instruction pointer, PROCPTR a procedure pointer, EXCM an exception description, SPC a space, CON a constant, OL an operand list, DD a data definition, VAR and PTR the general forms. Ordered longest-first so that SPC does not take the front of SPCPTR. IBM's functional reference documents the instruction set only and does not describe the language itself, so the declaration syntax is taken from Svalgaard, MI Programming (COMMON 408250 and 408251).
patterns.name: support.type.mi

patterns.comment: An identifier followed by a parenthesis, such as a built-in or a typed declaration attribute.
